methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Uptool operates in Robotics & Manufacturing, a sector populated by ten identified peers spanning one public company (277810.KQ) and eight private entities including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics. The target's stage, current valuation, and total capital raised remain undisclosed, limiting the precision of stage-specific analysis.

Peer-median valuation methodology proved inapplicable to this engagement. The Robotics & Manufacturing peer universe, while containing ten same-sector comparables, yielded insufficient clustering when filtered by stage alignment, adjacent-stage proximity, or similar valuation tier. Specifically, zero same-stage matches, zero adjacent-stage matches, and zero similar-tier matches were identified—falling below the three-datapoint minimum required for robust median triangulation. A sector-wide median approach was rejected to avoid false precision.

Without sufficient narrow-peer density, this valuation lacks triangulation support through standard comparable company methods. Meaningful analysis would require either: disclosure of Uptool's stage and prior funding history to enable tighter peer cohort construction; or access to financial performance metrics (revenue, EBITDA multiples) that could anchor DCF or precedent transaction frameworks. The current data constraints preclude a defensible valuation range. Analysts should recommend gathering stage-specific context before pursuing further valuation work on this target.
